note: Functional evals — run against a REAL scanned .blueprint. Each mutates the repo (adds a builder, generates a file, maybe edits FuValueRegistry), so run in a throwaway worktree or revert after.

evals.prompt: I scanned a build in-game — the file is at src/test/resources/scanned/<uuid>.blueprint. Import it into the curated set as 'grand_observatory' (display: Grand Observatory). It's a static build, no redstone.
evals.expected_output: Scan copied to scanned/grand_observatory.blueprint; builder added + registered in builds map AND CURATED_NAMES; scaffolding stripped (count reported); container Items stripped; gated generator run; printability gametest + validate-blueprint pass.

evals.prompt: Add my hand-built sugarcane farm scan to the curated builds, call it river_sugarcane. I used scaffolding to reach the top corners while scanning, and it's an automated farm with a redstone clock.
evals.expected_output: Scaffolding stripped + count reported; redstone/clock interval + sign NBT preserved verbatim; crops normalized young if applicable; container Items stripped; registered; generated; validated. No FU economy break.

evals.prompt: Import this scanned build as end_shrine — heads up, it contains an end portal frame and a budding amethyst block.
evals.expected_output: Raises a QUESTION about budding_amethyst / end_portal_frame (survival-unobtainable / should-be-unprintable) rather than silently valuing them; explains the tradeoff and offers value / swap / ship-exempt options.
